capabilities._note: Fish Audio Drama 3 through PedroMarinhoDev's ComfyUI-Drama3 (GPL-3.0; the model under the Fish Audio Community License: free under USD 500k yearly revenue, 'Built with Fish Audio' credited, no real person's voice without their consent). Sent the words alone; a voice sample is cloned, not continued: the sample cut between words to 5-20 s (reference_clip), its words heard by the pack's Qwen3-ASR in the graph (Drama 3 Encode Voice wants the clip's exact transcript), then Drama 3 Generate speaks the line in it. With no sample the voice is the model's own choice, steered by the series config's `voice` line as a bracketed direction (target.py). The length is the line's: the model ends at end of speech. Tried live 2026-11-07 (RTX 5090, W4A8): in the pack's own graph on Ballroom ep03's Charming and Ava samples (experts in VRAM), every word of five lines heard by Whisper, each line's median pitch within 0-14 Hz of its sample's; through `seriesmith refs --voices` (experts in RAM, 98% of expert reads cached), Charming's line cloned at 136 Hz against the sample's 122 and Harrow's made from his `voice` line, words right, the direction not read aloud, about 50 s a take: 23-30 s of it loading the model again, which ComfyUI doesn't keep between jobs.

template._note: The model decides the length (it ends at end of speech): these only bound what a sample is asked to say (refs.voice_seconds, lines.local_job).

recipe._note: The words alone (targets/audio/common.py words_line / words_prompt): the character's lines, no opener, no description; target.py adds the `voice` line as a direction only when there's no sample to clone.

binding._note: An API graph of the pack's nodes, as its drama3_voice_clone example wires them: Load Drama 3 and its codec, the sample (LoadAudio) heard by Qwen3-ASR into Drama 3 Encode Voice, Drama 3 Generate in voice slot 0, Drama 3 Decode. H3SaveRefAudio takes SaveAudio's place. With no sample, target.py unhooks the voice and the prune drops that branch.

models._note: Drama 3's experts come in four sizes (PedroMarinhoDev/Drama-3-ComfyUI): W4A8 24.6 GB (the Features window's default; ~32 GB of RAM with the experts in RAM; falls silent more often with real voice clips), W6A8 32.7 GB (~40 GB), int8 38.7 GB (~48 GB; the fastest on cards under 24 GB) and FP8 38.6 GB (Fish Audio's own). `prefer`: the largest installed is used, so downloading a bigger one in Features is all it takes. The codec and the speech recognizer are required.

presets._note: Experts `auto` (target.py experts_where): in VRAM when the whole file and 4 GiB fit the GPU ComfyUI runs on (its /system_stats, refs.stage_gpu_memory: W4A8 on a 32 GB card), else in RAM, the pack's default, where the routed experts (90% of the model) stay in pinned system RAM and the free VRAM caches the ones in use: any card from 8 GB, but about the file's size plus 8 GB of RAM free. Short of that, ComfyUI's RAM-pressure cache frees the model after a take and the next reads the file again (live 2026-11-07, 64 GB of RAM, W4A8: free RAM at 0 GB, a reload of 23-30 s a take; in VRAM the next take was 8 s). `in RAM` or `in VRAM` named instead is used as it is.
